humanities_role_explanation: Designed specifically to evaluate graduate-level and expert-level historical knowledge and comprehension across a vast array of global historical societies, utilizing structured data from the Seshat Global History Databank.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Textual questions and answers framed in a four-choice multiple-choice format based on historical datasets.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Testing factual recall of expert-level global history, specifically societal structures, characteristics, and temporal-regional facts through a four-choice multiple-choice question-answering format.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Specifically focused on the domain of global history rather than general-purpose multi-task evaluation.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Evaluates models from the Gemini, OpenAI (GPT-4-Turbo), and Llama (Llama-3.1-8B) families.

quantitative_metrics.note: Evaluates model performance using balanced accuracy.

published_after_march_2023.note: Published as part of the NeurIPS 2024 conference.

summary: This paper introduces HiST-LLM, a benchmark based on the Seshat Global History Databank designed to evaluate the historical knowledge of Large Language Models at a graduate level. It spans 36,000 data points across 600 historical societies, covering diverse world regions and eras from the Neolithic to the Industrial Revolution. The benchmark reveals that while state-of-the-art LLMs outperform random guessing, they still fall significantly short of human expert comprehension.
key_findings: Tested LLMs achieve a balanced accuracy ranging from 33.6% (Llama-3.1-8B) to 46.0% (GPT-4-Turbo) in a four-choice format, compared to a random baseline of 25%. LLMs perform better on earlier historical periods and show regional imbalances, with the Americas having the highest accuracy and Oceania and Sub-Saharan Africa having the lowest among advanced models.
facets_explanation: The HiST-LLM benchmark is constructed from a subset of the Seshat Global History Databank, a structured database describing historical societies compiled by history experts and graduate research assistants. Answering the four-choice questions requires external historical knowledge not contained within the prompt. The text does not discuss how disagreement among the original Seshat coders or benchmark builders was handled.
